result.result:
Autodoc now documents members that stack `@classmethod` on `@property`. The related tests pass on Python 3.9.25, apart from one unrelated failure explained below. Nothing is committed.

**Root cause:** on a class, `getattr(cls, name)` runs the class property and returns its result rather than a `property` object. So autodoc never saw a property. When the member list was built the value was usually `None`, and the member was dropped as having no docstring. `PropertyDocumenter` didn't recognise it either.

**Fix:**
- **New helper:** `getclassproperty(cls, name)` in `sphinx/util/inspect.py` searches the class and its base classes for a `classmethod` wrapping a property, and returns the property. Inherited class properties are therefore found too.
- **Member listing** (`sphinx/ext/autodoc/importer.py`): `get_class_members` now uses the property object instead of the evaluated value. That makes the docstring visible and covers autosummary, which builds its member lists with the same function.
- **`PropertyDocumenter`** (`sphinx/ext/autodoc/__init__.py`): it accepts class properties, uses the property itself as the object to document, and adds `:classmethod:` to the directive. `:abstractmethod:` and type hints still work. An `.. autoproperty::` aimed at something that isn't a property behaves as it did before.
- **`py:property` directive** (`sphinx/domains/python.py`): new `:classmethod:` option, which renders as "class property".
- **Docs:** the new option is described in `doc/usage/restructuredtext/domains.rst`, and there is a CHANGES entry for #9445.

**Tests:**
- A `prop2` class property was added to `tests/roots/test-ext-autodoc/target/properties.py`, only defined on Python 3.9+.
- New tests: `test_class_properties` (autoproperty), `test_pyproperty_classmethod` (domain) and `test_getclassproperty` (inspect). `test_getclassproperty` covers inherited, overridden, plain-property and plain-classmethod cases.
- The expected output of the autoclass `test_properties` was updated.
- Ran the autodoc test files (main, autoproperty, autoclass, autoattribute, automodule), plus the domain, autosummary and inspect tests: 215 passed, 1 failed.

**The one failure:** `tests/test_util_inspect.py` imports `_testcapi`, which isn't installed in `.venv`, so I ran that file against a temporary empty stand-in. `test_isattributedescriptor` needs things from the real module, so it fails there; it fails the same way without these changes.

**End-to-end check:** I built a small project modelled on the issue's demo. The metaclass, base-class, subclass, inherited and abstract class properties all rendered, with the abstract one shown as "abstract class property".

I changed some of the subagent's first pass myself:
- It only checked the class's own `__dict__`, which missed inherited class properties.
- It made `autoproperty` give up silently on anything that isn't a property.
- It extended `isclassmethod` in a way nothing used, so I took that out.
